title: DxMessaging
description:
Connect gameplay systems without direct references between senders and receivers. DxMessaging provides synchronous, type-safe untargeted, targeted, and broadcast messages. Lifecycle-managed registration tokens pair subscriptions with components and dependency-injection scopes. Message Monitor, Flow Graph, Inspector overlays, and runtime diagnostics make routes visible while you develop. Struct messages keep steady-state dispatch allocation-free. Optional samples cover Zenject, VContainer, and Reflex.

DxMessaging is free and will remain free forever. No paid editions, paid upgrades, or feature charges.

AI assistance disclosure: DxMessaging began as an original project around 2014 and remains actively developed and used today. Over the past two years, I (wallstop) have been using LLMs to help improve the library's quality and performance, expand its tests, and create user-facing documentation. There is always a human in the loop: I actively review all changes and read through all user-facing copy. I share this so you can make an informed decision about using the project.
aiDescription: OpenAI models starting with GPT-5, used through Codex, and Anthropic models starting with Opus 4, used through Claude Code, have assisted with substantial portions of the code, tests, and documentation. I (wallstop) review all changes for accuracy and correctness and read all user-facing copy. Artwork is minimal and includes AI-generated SVGs. Product screenshots show the actual editor tooling.
